newsitem.title: USA: GE, Harris set energy management effort.
newsitem.headline: GE, Harris set energy management effort.

text.p: General Electric Co's GE Power Systems said Monday it formed a venture with Harris Corp to provide digitally-based, intelligent energy management systems and services to electric utilities and industrial users.
These information technology systems automate and integrate power systems for optimal efficiency, it said.

They also enable electrical producers and users to better capitalize on opportunities to buy, sell and manage power in a deregulated market, it added. The venture, to be 51 percent owned by GE, is called GE Harris Energy Systems.

GE said first-year sales for the new company are expected to reach $100 million, establishing GE Harris Energy Systems as a global leader in the energy management market, currently estimated to be $1 billion annually.
The trend toward deregulated power around the world is expected to drive the energy management market to several billion dollars annually within the next decade, it added.
GE said no financial arrangements besides parent company ownership were disclosed.

It said the venture will design, manufacture and market computer control centers and other electronics that help utilities identify the most cost-effective method of dispatching power, track power quality, simulate outages and recommend timely actions to optimize operations.

Also included is Harris's world-leading distribution automation product line that allows the remote measuring of voltages, currents, power flows and temperatures while providing a data link to a central energy management system.
GE Harris Energy Systems will be headquartered in Melbourne, Fla., with engineering and manufacturing operations in Melbourne and Calgary, Canada.
The new company will initially include about 650 employees from GE and Harris and will have access to the product development and technical resources of both parent companies.
GE said Paul T. Armstrong, most recently from GE Power Systems, has been named president of GE Harris Energy Systems.
